subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram provider intermittently stalls despite stable direct Bot API connectivity

question: Should OpenClaw accept a shared scheme-aware Telegram/SOCKS proxy fix now, and should that happen by repairing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84582 or replacing it with a broader maintainer-owned proxy repair?
rationale: The source and Undici contract make the SOCKS proxy failure plausible, but the durable fix affects compatibility-sensitive shared proxy behavior and still needs live Telegram proof.

options.title: Require Shared Proxy Repair
options.body: Ask for or create a scheme-aware repair covering explicit and env SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS proxy modes with tests and live Telegram proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Defer For More Live Data
options.body: Keep this issue open without accepting a proxy change until the reporter or maintainer captures a current-main SOCKS5 stall trace from the affected environment.

options.title: Limit To Existing Workarounds
options.body: Decline a shared proxy behavior change for now and document supported DNS/proxy configuration guidance, leaving this issue open only if fresh evidence shows that guidance fails.

recommendation.title: Require Shared Proxy Repair
recommendation.body: Ask for or create a scheme-aware repair covering explicit and env SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS proxy modes with tests and live Telegram proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest provenance connects this decision to the shared Undici proxy helper and Telegram proxy/fallback behavior where steipete has central history.
